:::{#def-diagonalizable}
#### Diagonalizable matrix

A $p \times p$ matrix $\matr{A}$ is **diagonalizable**
if it is similar (@def-similar) to a diagonal matrix (@def-diagonal-matrix):
$\matr{A} = \matr{X} \matr{\Lambda} \matr{X}^{-1}$
for some invertible $\matr{X}$ and diagonal $\matr{\Lambda}$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-diagonalizable}
#### Diagonalizable and not

- $\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$ is diagonalizable,
  being similar to $\operatorname{diag}(3, 1)$ (@exm-similar).
- $\matr{J} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ is not.
  Its only eigenvalue is $0$ (@exm-eigenspace),
  so a diagonal matrix similar to it would have only $0$ on its diagonal
  (@thm-eigen-triangular, @thm-similar-eigenvalues),
  that is, would be $\matr{0}_{2 \times 2}$;
  but then $\matr{J} = \matr{X}\,\matr{0}_{2 \times 2}\,\matr{X}^{-1} = \matr{0}_{2 \times 2}$, which it is not.

:::
